title: Explain what statistics is, the four phases of a statistical study, its functions and importance (including in banking) and its limitations
Tell population from sample, parameter from statistic, and variates (discrete or continuous) from attributes
Choose between primary and secondary data and between a census and a sample survey, and name the usual collection methods
Classify data on the four bases (qualitative, quantitative, geographical, chronological) and as one-way, two-way or multi-way tables
Build and read frequency distributions: class limits, width, mark, boundaries, relative, percentage, density and cumulative frequencies
Explain why samples are used, the notation for populations and samples, judgement versus random sampling, and how biased samples arise
Distinguish simple random, systematic, stratified and cluster sampling, sampling with and without replacement, and choose the suitable method
Describe a sampling distribution and the standard error, and compute the standard error and z value of a sample mean
Use the normal sampling distribution of the mean, for normal and non-normal populations, and apply the central limit theorem
Apply the finite population multiplier and the sampling fraction rule, and judge the trade-off between sample size and standard error
Compute the arithmetic mean of raw and grouped data, the combined mean, a corrected mean and a missing value, and judge its merits and limits
Compute the geometric and harmonic means, say when each is appropriate, and relate them to the arithmetic mean
Find the median and the quartiles of raw and grouped data
Find the mode of raw and grouped data, relate mean, median and mode, and choose between the averages
Explain absolute and relative measures of dispersion and compute the range, quartile deviation and mean deviation with their coefficients
Compute the standard deviation, variance and coefficient of variation, and use them to compare consistency
Describe skewness and kurtosis, read the direction of skew from the averages and moments, and name leptokurtic, mesokurtic and platykurtic shapes
